operations.observation_text: H7760A sim ("to set, place, appoint") + H3820A leb ("inner man, mind, will, heart -- seat of resolution/determination") -- a deliberate act of will crystallizing internally, not a passing preference: Daniel SETS this UPON his own heart/mind as a fixed purpose.
operations.description_text: Daniel's own inward resolve, self-originating, not stated as prompted by any outside party -- the fixed purpose not to defile himself with the king's food and wine.

targets.detail: the king's food and the wine he drank (1:8a) -- the specific object the resolve is directed against

operations.observation_text: H0559 amar in its purposive sense ("to say, to intend") -- Daniel's resolve of 1:8 moves outward into concrete address to the authority actually in a position to grant it.
operations.description_text: Daniel takes the initiative himself, approaching the steward directly rather than waiting -- continuation of the same resolve now expressed as action.

targets.detail: the steward Daniel addresses directly

operations.observation_text: H5254G nasah ("to test, try, prove, put to the proof") -- Daniel frames his own request as something to be PROVEN, not merely asserted; a disposition of confidence willing to risk objective disproof.
operations.description_text: The specific terms of Daniel's proposal (ten days, vegetables and water) put to the steward as a trial he is willing to be judged by.

targets.detail: the steward, whose decision the proposal seeks to influence

operations.observation_text: H7200G ra'ah in its passive/evidentiary sense ("to appear, be seen, present oneself") -- Daniel deliberately names the evidentiary standard (visible appearance) the steward is to judge by.
operations.description_text: Continuation of the same proposal: Daniel stakes the outcome explicitly on what the steward will visibly observe, evidencing confidence in the expected result.

targets.detail: the steward, named as the one who will observe and judge

operations.observation_text: H0995 biyn ("to discern, understand, consider") applied to H2377 chazon (vision, specifically prophetic/revelatory) and H2472 chalom (dream) -- a distinct interior faculty of revelatory discernment, individuating Daniel from the other three.
operations.description_text: Daniel's own additional gift beyond the shared endowment of 1:17a. Whether this too is implicitly sourced to God (as 1:17a explicitly states) or presented as Daniel's own innate faculty is a live reading question -- 1:17b's own verb is "had" [possessive/stative], not a repeated "was given"; kept as retain_referential rather than asserting the divine-source reading as settled fact.

sources.detail: no source verb repeated in 1:17b itself (contrast 1:17a's explicit "God gave"); possible implicit continuation of the same divine source is a live reading, not asserted here

operations.observation_text: H2617A chesed ("goodness, kindness, faithfulness") + H7356B racham ("compassion") -- an interior disposition of kindness/tenderness. CORRECTED on closing.set/debate-quality-validation re-examination (2026-08-07): the Hebrew idiom "gave X favor in the sight of Y" most directly asserts a favorable OUTCOME/circumstance for Daniel (Ashpenaz's treatment of him), and only secondarily implies Ashpenaz's own felt interior state -- extending sourcing from a stated outcome to an interior disposition is exactly what operation.set/source-vs-enablement warns must be flagged, not assumed.
operations.description_text: Kept as retain (genuinely inner-being, not merely outcome) because 1:10's immediately-following stated fear presupposes Ashpenaz DOES feel something toward Daniel -- the fear only makes narrative sense if a real, felt favorable disposition toward Daniel is already in tension with it. But the outcome-vs-interior distinction is now named explicitly here rather than the interior reading being asserted as simply/directly stated by 1:9 alone.

targets.detail: Daniel, toward whom the favor/compassion is directed

operations.reconciliation_note: closing.set/debate-quality-validation representative-sample re-examination (2026-08-07) found this entry asserted the interior-disposition reading of 1:9's idiom as simply stated, without flagging that operation.set/source-vs-enablement requires exactly this outcome-vs-interior distinction to be named when extending a non-human party's stated sourcing from an outcome to an interior state. Corrected: same decision (retain) and same source/target, but observation_text/description_text now name the distinction and the textual basis (1:10's own following fear) for keeping the interior reading rather than silently asserting it.

quality_checks.phenomenon-actually-underlies-it: Yes -- phenomenon.set/1:9 already established this as Ashpenaz's own stated disposition; the correction only refines the operation's own sourcing language, not the underlying phenomenon.
quality_checks.source-target-not-invented: Unchanged -- source/target are the same as before (God / Daniel), exactly who 1:9 itself names.
quality_checks.observation-uses-full-lexical-range: Unchanged lexical grounding (chesed/racham), with the outcome-vs-interior distinction now named explicitly.

operations.description_text: Kept explicitly as retain_referential (inferred, not stated) -- the text does not itself assert this causal reading; it is this pass's own default reading of the sequence, on record as such rather than disguised as settled fact.
